- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for high sentiment periods.
- If model shows sharp upward spikes (e.g., >2x recent mean), apply downward correction to prevent overshoot; especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- In low sentiment (≤ 0.33) or negative sentiment periods, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.
- Model frequently overcorrects after sharp declines — if recent history shows a drop followed by a rebound, forecast should be conservative and lag slightly behind true trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) — apply a smoothing decay factor to reduce initial overconfidence.
- When sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating 0.33/1.00), model should avoid extreme outliers and favor mean-reversion anchors.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model should not forecast upward unless sentiment strongly supports it (≥ 0.80).
